title: The data is very preliminary, but Vulcan failure may not be due to BE-4 engines
gist: ULA's Vulcan return-to-flight launch failed due to low core-stage performance just after liftoff; preliminary data cited by two sources points to a vehicle-side propellant-feed issue rather than Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, though one engine may have run at reduced thrust. The grounding (likely 6+ months) hits the Space Force and Amazon Leo, and a BE-4 root cause would also delay New Glenn and NASA's Artemis plans.

insights.claim: ULA's Vulcan return-to-flight launch failed after low booster (core stage) performance just after liftoff caused stage separation at too low an altitude and below the minimum velocity needed to reach orbit; telemetry and the mission were lost about 10 minutes into flight.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A failed national-security-class launcher deepens US heavy-lift capacity constraints; watch ULA owners and dependent payload customers.
insights.quote: early indications are that just after liftoff, the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance, resulting in stage separation occurring when the vehicle was low in altitude and below minimal velocity to reach orbit
insights.locator: United Launch Alliance (ULA) confirmed Tuesday morning

insights.claim: ULA confirmed that Vulcan's Centaur V upper stage and its solid rocket boosters performed nominally during the failed flight, isolating the problem to the core stage.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Narrows the failure to the core stage/BE-4 propulsion area, which is what links the investigation to Blue Origin.
insights.locator: The launch company also confirmed reporting by Ars

insights.claim: The failed mission was the fifth Vulcan flight since its January 2024 debut; two prior flights suffered solid rocket booster nozzle issues that the vehicle compensated for, and the second of those grounded Vulcan for nine months.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Vulcan's reliability record is now weak across multiple subsystems, raising customer risk perception and potential manifest shifts.
insights.locator: This was the fifth flight of the Vulcan rocket

themes.theme: Preliminary root cause: vehicle vs. BE-4

insights.claim: According to two independent sources' reading of preliminary data, the Vulcan failure is currently believed to have originated on the launch-vehicle side rather than inside Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, possibly in the systems feeding methane and liquid oxygen propellant to the engines.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: If confirmed, this partially exonerates Blue Origin's BE-4 and limits contagion to New Glenn; still very preliminary.

insights.claim: ULA engineers are examining whether one of Vulcan's two BE-4 engines dropped to lower thrust shortly after liftoff and never returned to full throttle, with high-zoom tracking video appearing to show one engine dimmer than the other after booster jettison nearly two minutes into flight.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: An engine-level thrust deficit would shift blame toward the engine or its feed system; the answer determines who bears schedule and cost impact.
insights.locator: ULA engineers are looking at the possibility

insights.claim: An asymmetric shutdown of Vulcan's two BE-4 engines may have contributed to the sudden attitude motion seen in ULA's telemetry-driven animation near stage separation.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Another data point investigators will use to discriminate between engine and vehicle-side failure modes.
insights.locator: ULA engineers are looking at the possibility

insights.claim: ULA and Blue Origin are tightly holding information on the Vulcan failure; sources describe the ULA-led, FAA-overseen investigation as incredibly complicated and still in early stages, and the author stresses no definitive conclusions should be drawn.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Expect a long, opaque investigation; headline risk persists until a root cause is formally announced.
insights.quote: Again, this information is preliminary, and no definitive conclusions can or should be drawn.
insights.locator: Information about the Vulcan failure is being closely held

insights.claim: The Vulcan failure is likely to sideline the rocket for at least six months and probably longer, worsening an already deteriorating US launch-capacity crisis.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Constrained US launch supply strengthens pricing power and share for alternative providers and delays satellite deployment timelines.
insights.quote: This latest setback is likely to sideline Vulcan for at least half a year, and probably longer.
insights.locator: This latest setback is likely to sideline Vulcan

insights.claim: The US Space Force, with national security payloads waiting on Vulcan, and Amazon, which had more than a dozen Amazon Leo constellation launches on Vulcan's 2027 manifest, are the customers most impacted by Vulcan's grounding.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Amazon Leo deployment schedule (and its competitiveness vs. other broadband constellations) is at risk; watch for Amazon re-booking launches elsewhere.
insights.locator: This latest setback is likely to sideline Vulcan

themes.theme: Blue Origin and New Glenn exposure

insights.claim: Blue Origin's New Glenn uses a similar, slightly more powerful BE-4 variant and suffered a catastrophic ground-test failure in May attributed to a BE-4 main oxygen valve, so any BE-4 link to Vulcan's failure carries cross-program risk.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Shared engine architecture creates correlated failure risk across two US heavy-lift vehicles.
insights.locator: Critically, ULA did not provide any specific information

insights.claim: Blue Origin is aiming to return New Glenn to flight as early as January, says a modified BE-4 main oxygen valve completed qualification testing, is being rolled out across the engine fleet, and expects to finish its anomaly investigation later in November.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Near-term catalyst: New Glenn return-to-flight timing, contingent on Vulcan root cause not implicating the BE-4.
insights.quote: Our modified valve has already been incorporated into engines slated for upcoming flights, and we are now rolling it out across the remaining fleet
insights.locator: There are potentially serious implications for Blue Origin

insights.claim: If the Vulcan failure is ultimately traced to the BE-4 engine, New Glenn's return to flight would almost certainly be delayed, setting back NASA, which relies on New Glenn for much of the heavy lifting for its Artemis Program and Moon Base.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A BE-4 root cause would ripple into NASA lunar timelines and the broader US heavy-lift supply.
insights.locator: If Vulcan's failure were ultimately due to a problem with the BE-4 engine
